note: SNG-663 §2d. Flat, per load that sells (a traveller selling in person pays once per visit), in shards. Scaled against today's runs (56 to 130 shards a pass on Silas's holds) so a fee matters at the margin and never eats a run. Only the two powers whose own verbs already steal, smuggle, extort or levy by force are corrupt: the Undercount (a thieves' guild) and the Firstsight Barony (cruel, toll and levy). Everyone else's wardens are as their temper says.

power_millbrook_council.line: Two shards to the Council's box by the well, and a stall till dusk. Millbrook likes you well enough to want you back.

power_keelmouth_slip.line: The Slip's clerk takes three shards and a look at your hands; anyone who's worked a rope pays and gets a smile.

power_flesh_temple.line: Four shards to the Temple, paid into a hand that has been trained until it is very steady.

power_harmonic_heights.line: Five shards and a tuning: the Terrace wardens strike a fork over your load and listen. Paid and in tune, you may sell.

power_glass_assembly.line: Five shards, weighed against the Assembly's glass and written into the ledger in front of you. The Assembly is patient and it is exact.

power_hollow_court.line: Six shards, posted a yard high on the Asking Floor, and not one shard more or less for anyone. The Court's fairness is the frightening kind.

power_seraphic_orders.line: Six shards to the almoners, and your goods blessed whether you asked or not. The Orders tithe what they allow.

power_radiant_plateau.line: Six shards at the Edge District's lamp-post, and a Plateau warden's opinion of your goods, which is not negotiable.

power_grand_lattice.line: Eight shards, deducted at Intake before you knew you'd agreed. The Lattice's schedule has already decided you are selling, and to whom.

power_undercount.line: Four shards to sell in the Hundred Markets, officially. A Counter's man will tell you what it is today, and today it depends on you.

power_firstsight_barony.line: Ten shards to the Baron's wardens at the market gate, they say, and the Baron sees perhaps four of them.
